clue.text: Boring man taking on financial commitments

indicators.note: one piece takes on, or adds, the next one after it

parts.note: Ted is a common man's name, short for Edward
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A man is weighed down by loans and debts, which makes him dull company.
explanation.definitionFit: Something boring is dull and wearisome, which is what tedious means.

clue.text: Got less to draw on before the beginning of December

parts.note: to tap is to draw on a supply, as in tapping resources
ere is a poetic word for before

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone drew on their savings until early December and had less left.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that narrows or diminishes gradually becomes less, the sense of the answer.

clue.text: Three notes read out and put down

parts.note: D, E and G are three musical notes

indicators.note: out signals the word read is put out of its order

explanation.surface: A musician reads three notes aloud and then sets them down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read out' suggests speaking, but 'out' rearranges READ to RADE.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone down is to humiliate or belittle them.

clue.text: Some of the very poor risk growing such a root

indicators.note: some of the words means just a part of their run of letters is taken

explanation.surface: Very poor people risk cultivating a certain root crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Orris root comes from certain irises and is used in perfume and gin.

clue.text: This would always run to time

definitions.text: This would always run to time

parts.words: This would always run to time
parts.note: 'run to time' sounds like a punctual train, but sand running through a glass is what marks the time

explanation.definitionFit: An hourglass measures time by sand trickling from one bulb to the other.

clue.text: A priest distributed certain cash

indicators.note: letters handed out and spread around end up in a new order

explanation.surface: A priest hands out a sum of money among the parish poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges the seven letters of A PRIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A piastre is a coin or unit of currency used in Egypt and other parts of the Middle East, so a particular kind of money.

clue.text: Takes up a questionable position?

parts.note: taking up a posture for an artist, with a nod to putting a question

explanation.definitionFit: A model strikes attitudes, and one also puts questions, so the word covers both.

clue.text: Beautiful stone resulting from a laboratory bloomer

parts.note: an aster is a flower, something that blooms

explanation.surface: A lovely gem came out of a lab's mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder, but it means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a smooth white mineral prized for carving ornaments.

clue.text: A player's shaky performance

parts.note: suggests a nervous musician, but means the deliberate trembling effect a musician produces

explanation.definitionFit: This is a wavering musical effect from rapid repetition of a note, deliberately shaky.

clue.text: Without any aim to make it permanent

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
less means without, as in a pointless suffix

explanation.surface: Someone without a goal stays that way forever.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as a goal plus a suffix meaning lacking, though 'Without' comes first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that never finishes lasts forever, as permanent things do.

clue.text: The swine with a club for a chunk of metal

parts.note: a swine is a pig
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A pig armed with a club is swapped for a lump of metal.
explanation.walkthrough: Pig iron is crude iron cast in blocks straight from the blast furnace.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig iron is cast in oblong blocks called pigs, so it is a lump of crude metal.

clue.text: Instil respect in children for such plants

indicators.note: to instil something is to put it into something else, here into the word for children

parts.note: seed is an old word for offspring or descendants
awe is deep reverence or respect

explanation.surface: Parents are told to teach their children some respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'children' as seed is the biblical sense of offspring or descendants; 'Instil' is the container signal, with 'in' just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaweeds are marine algae, loosely regarded as plants of the sea.

clue.text: They give directions by the way

definitions.text: They give directions by the way

parts.words: They give directions by the way
parts.note: 'by the way' looks like a throwaway aside but means at the side of the road, where these direction boards stand

explanation.definitionFit: Signposts along a road tell drivers which way to go, placed literally beside the way.

clue.text: A sound opener to admire

indicators.note: sound means the word is heard rather than spelt, so its pronunciation is what counts

parts.note: a door is an opener, the thing that opens to let you in

explanation.surface: A good opening move earns praise.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'a door' is heard as the answer, so the second half is spelt DORE.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire someone deeply is to love or worship them.

clue.text: Caused by two people singing a round

parts.note: a duet is a piece performed by two singers
the letter O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Something happened because a pair of singers performed a round together.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'round' looks like a sung canon here, but it just means the circular letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: If one thing happens owing to another, it was brought about by it.

clue.text: Turn to the woman's way as an alternative

indicators.note: turning the little word to reverses its two letters

parts.note: her is the possessive meaning belonging to a woman
wise is an old word for manner or way, as in 'in no wise'

explanation.surface: A man turns to his partner's way of doing things instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise means in another way or else, offering an alternative.

clue.text: Bringing down this high-flier brought trouble in the main

definitions.text: Bringing down this high-flier brought trouble in the main

parts.words: Bringing down this high-flier brought trouble in the main
parts.note: refers to Coleridge's Ancient Mariner, who shot a great sea bird and brought a curse on his ship; 'the main' is the open sea

explanation.definitionFit: In Coleridge's poem the sailor kills the great ocean bird and his whole crew suffers for it at sea.

clue.text: Mad, but agrees to offer a sweetener

indicators.note: mad means crazy, so the letters go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: An angry person nonetheless agrees to offer some sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar extracted from sugar beet is used to sweeten food.

clue.text: He stops at break very speedily!

indicators.note: to break the words is to smash them up and reassemble the pieces in another order

explanation.surface: A man halts at a rest break, after travelling at great speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' rearranges all nine letters of HE STOPS AT, though 'stops' and 'break' both seem to belong to a story about pausing.
explanation.definitionFit: Posthaste means with all possible speed, originally as fast as the post riders went.

clue.text: Little page wanting second dish of food

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for page
the latter is the second of two things mentioned

explanation.surface: A young page boy wants a second helping of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A platter is a large flat plate for serving food.

clue.text: Puts in order for benches

definitions.meaning: long wooden seats with high backs

explanation.definitionFit: The word means sorting things out, and as a plural noun, long high-backed wooden seats.

clue.text: Exact what one is entitled to?

definitions.meaning: exact here is the adjective meaning correct or accurate
an entitlement, something you may claim by law or morality

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both correct, as in the correct time, and an entitlement, as in human rights.

clue.text: Contort the face, appalling one

parts.note: grim means dreadful or appalling
an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Someone pulls a face at a dreadful sight.
explanation.definitionFit: To grimace is to twist the features in pain or disgust.

clue.text: Get thin perhaps — and get more tense

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Losing weight might also make you more tense.
explanation.definitionFit: To tighten is to become tauter or tenser.

clue.text: Behind a measure albeit with some hesitation

parts.note: FT is the abbreviation for foot or feet, a measure of length
er is the sound people make when they hesitate

explanation.surface: Someone falls behind on a measurement, stammering a little.
explanation.definitionFit: Behind and the answer both mean later in order or following on.

clue.text: Standing out for rise maybe - >smart, that!

indicators.note: maybe suggests the word could be something else, here its letters rearranged

parts.note: to smart is to sting with pain

explanation.surface: Holding out for a pay rise hurts, the clue says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges RISE to RESI, followed by STING. The stray '- >' in the clue is a transcription glitch, not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing out against something means holding firm and refusing to give way.

clue.text: Lines a boy up to bring the water

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, a set of lines

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy brings lines up to the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Rydal Water is a small lake in the English Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Rydal Water is a lake in Cumbria, so a body of water.

clue.text: Against going in alone to work out

indicators.note: going in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: sole means only or alone
V is short for versus, meaning against

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to joining a group prefers to exercise alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To work out a puzzle or problem is to find its answer.

clue.text: Everyone inside joined and corresponded

indicators.note: inside places the word for everyone within the word for joined

parts.note: tied means fastened or joined together
all means every person

explanation.surface: Everybody was joined together and kept in touch by letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corresponded' suggests writing letters, but here it means matched up.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts that agree are said to match or correspond, the sense of the answer here.

clue.text: Daring to inflame a group of conservationists

parts.note: to gall is to chafe, irritate or make sore
NT is the National Trust, the British charity that conserves historic buildings and countryside

explanation.surface: It takes nerve to anger a band of environmental campaigners.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British heritage charity, abbreviated NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallant means brave and spirited, so daring in the face of danger.

clue.text: It's about time to correct the letters

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
a spell is a period of time

explanation.surface: It is high time someone corrected the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' suggests mail, but it means the letters of a word, which are put right by spelling them again.
explanation.definitionFit: To spell a word again, especially differently, is to put its sequence of letters right.

clue.text: A need or requirement for school

indicators.note: the requirement here is that the letters be reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A school is a necessity or a need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requirement' is a loose signal to rearrange A NEED OR. Roedean is a famous girls' boarding school near Brighton, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Roedean is a well-known independent girls' boarding school on the Sussex coast.
